summary: Mount Ascutney summit lookout: a 1940 steel tower later shortened to a 25-ft observation tower in the state park; the association's relocation claim is not confirmed by other sources.

facts.design: Steel fire tower, 54 ft as built in 1940; today's observation tower is shorter (25 ft)
facts.agency: Vermont Department of Forests, Parks & Recreation

access.note: Inside Mt. Ascutney State Park; summit reached by the paved Mountain Road and four trails. The sources give no rules for climbing the observation tower.

visit.trail_note: Four major trails, about 12 miles in total, start at the base and climb to the summit

Association lists a relocated Mount Ascutney observation tower as standing; no source read describes the move

notes_for_editor: Only the association's list (cite 3) says the tower was relocated, and the list gives no detail. The record's note that it moved 'a short way, to a new spot on the same site' could not be checked: the association's detail page is not in the cache, and no read source describes a move. The record's height_m 7.6 is the 25-ft figure from the state park for today's observation tower, converted to metres; the parent record (us-vt-mount-ascutney) carries the same 7.6 m against a 54-ft 1940 steel tower, so the parent height may need review. The parent also says 'relocated' while the association lists the original as 'Tower Gone'. A WebSearch summary attributed construction to CCC Company 129 (1933-1938); no page I could read states that, so it is not used. The county correction rests on the Forest Lookouts page, which reads 'Windsor County'; the association's list repeats the typo.
